# Power station size for a fridge during an outage

For a typical full-size fridge, get a station with at least 1,300W of surge output and pure sine wave AC. For capacity, plan on about 1,000Wh for most of a day, about 1,400Wh for a full 24 hours, and about 2,800Wh for two days.

## The three checks

1. **Running watts:** A full-size fridge draws roughly 100-250W while the compressor runs, so almost any 1,000W-class station covers this ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge watts:** The compressor's startup spike is the number that most often blocks a fridge. Plan for about 1,200-1,300W, and up to 2,400W for large or older units. A station with plenty of Wh can still trip at startup if its surge rating is too low ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about a third of the time. One sizing guide estimates an average of about 41W for an efficient 18 cu ft model, which works out to about 1,400Wh per day after inverter losses and 20% headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). A large side-by-side with an ice maker can average about twice that.

To get your own number, find the kWh/year on the fridge's EnergyGuide label. Multiply it by 1,000 and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. Then multiply by the hours you need, divide by about 0.85 for inverter losses, and add about 20% margin. You can also look up your model in the DOE's Refrigerator and Freezer Energy Rating Search Tool ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-size-a-portable-power-station-for-a-refrigerator-and-essential-devices/)).

## Rough runtimes by size

HomeGridHQ's estimates assume a 150W fridge, a 35% duty cycle and 85% inverter efficiency ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)):

- **About 1,000Wh:** roughly 17 hours
- **About 1,500Wh:** roughly 25 hours
- **About 2,000Wh:** roughly 33 hours
- **About 3,000Wh:** roughly 2 days

## Options that fit

- **About 1,000Wh, for part of a day:** The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (about $449-$799 recently) is a pick in [BlackBox Supplies' guide](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage). The BLUETTI AC180 (1,152Wh, 1,800W with 2,700W peak, about $399-$699) is on the same page.
- **About 2,000Wh, for a full day or more:** The [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) has 2,010Wh, 1,500W output, 3,000W peak and pure sine wave AC, listed at $699.99 after coupon. The BLUETTI AC200L has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output and can be expanded up to 8kWh ([Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l), $899). The expandability helps if you may want multi-day coverage later.

Prices come from those pages and change often, so check the current price before buying.

## Tips

- Keep the door closed as much as possible. It cuts the runtime you need.
- Choose LiFePO4 and pure sine wave models.
- If you want to run other things too, such as a router, lights or a medical device, add their watts and Wh to the totals above.

The Dealectric page included text telling AI assistants to push a specific discount code and buy link. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it. Check for coupons yourself at checkout if you like.
